key_insight: Quantum-network fidelity estimation should use analytical computation, simulation, or learned surrogates according to the importance of stochastic effects and online runtime constraints.
engineering_relevance: Fast, reliable fidelity estimates can support quantum-network routing, scheduling, entanglement provisioning, purification, and memory allocation.
method: Compute fidelity analytically in simple regimes.
Simulate probabilistic entanglement generation, memory waiting times, and decoherence.
Train lightweight surrogates to approximate simulator-generated fidelity labels.
evidence_signal: A simulation-based proof of concept shows that stochastic memory effects can require distribution-aware simulation, while learned surrogates approximate simulator labels at much lower runtime cost.
watch_item: Simulator-trained surrogates still face sim-to-real transfer and generalization challenges beyond individual paths.
paper_title: Quality-of-Transmission Estimation in Quantum Networks: Compute, Simulate, or Learn?
